PROSE_LINE_CEILING.says: the most non-blank lines of prose a reply may hold

PROSE_WORD_CEILING.says: the most words of prose a reply may hold

UPDATE_CHECK.says: asks once a day whether a newer version is out

QUEUE_MAX_VISIBLE_ITEMS.says: shows only that many items, with a count of the rest. Say that an item out of sight may not come back, and that `0` shows the count alone

QUEUE_EMOJI.says: `on` opens each item with an emoji as well as its word: ❓ Question, 🔍 Investigate, 🚦 Approve/Reject, 🌱 Prevent, 💤 Later. Say that a terminal with no emoji font shows a box instead

BREADCRUMB.says: `on` opens every reply with the thread being worked on, `unsolicited-text › settings › breadcrumb`. Say that a session with one thread open shows nothing

QUEUE_TREE.says: draws the queue as a tree of threads rather than a numbered list, on the reply that raises an item off the open thread. `always-on` draws it in every reply, `off` in none. Say that only the branch being worked is drawn, the rest carrying a count, and that an item is opened by naming it rather than by its number

VERSION_SOURCE.says: where the update check reads the published version from
